[New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_New_England_Patriots_season) 13 | ## Origin [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/41/1986_Jeno%27s_Pizza_-_37_-_Joe_Namath_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1986_Jeno's_Pizza_-_37_-_Joe_Namath_(cropped).jpg) The [New York Jets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_New_York_Jets_season) were the first AFL team to win a Super Bowl ( [III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_III)), upsetting the [Baltimore Colts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Baltimore_Colts_season) ## Game history [[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#cite_note-20) The Cowboys, Steelers, Broncos and the 49ers are tied for second with eight appearances apiece, reaching that milestone in this respective order. [Bill Belichick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Belichick) [owns the record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_ring#Most_Super_Bowl_rings) for the most Super Bowl wins (eight) and appearances (twelve: nine times as head coach, once as assistant head coach, and twice as defensive coordinator) by an individual. [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady) has the most Super Bowl starts (ten) and wins as a player (seven), while [Charles Haley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Haley) has the second-most wins among players with five. ### 1970s: Dominant franchises [[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#cite_note-30)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#cite_note-31) The Dolphins would repeat as league champions by winning [Super Bowl VIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_VIII) a year later with a 24–7 win over the Minnesota Vikings. ### 2010s: Patriots reign; parity in the NFC [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Tom_Brady_with_Vince_Lombardi_trophy.jpg/250px-Tom_Brady_with_Vince_Lombardi_trophy.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tom_Brady_with_Vince_Lombardi_trophy.jpg) The [New England Patriots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Patriots) postgame speech after [Super Bowl LI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LI), February 5, 2017[![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Super_Bowl_402EF3AA.jpg/250px-Super_Bowl_402EF3AA.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Super_Bowl_402EF3AA.jpg) The [Philadelphia Eagles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Eagles) are presented with the [Vince Lombardi Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_Lombardi_Trophy) after winning [Super Bowl LII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LII), February 4, 2018. [[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#cite_note-96) This became [Aaron Rodgers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Rodgers)' only Super Bowl victory. [[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#cite_note-97) This was the Giants' fourth Super Bowl victory. In [Super Bowl LI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LI), the first Super Bowl to end in overtime,[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#cite_note-115) the Atlanta Falcons led 28–3 late in the third quarter, but the Patriots came back to tie the game 28–28 with back-to-back touchdowns and two-point conversions, and the Patriots went on to win 34–28 in overtime. It was Tom Brady's 5th Super Bowl win and he was awarded his record fourth Super Bowl MVP, throwing a then-record 466 yards for 43 completions. In [Super Bowl LII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LII), the Philadelphia Eagles defeated the defending champion Patriots 41–33, ending a 57-year championship drought for the franchise.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#cite_note-121) [Nick Foles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Foles) won the Super Bowl MVP. ### 2020s: Beginning of the Chiefs' dominance [[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl#cite_note-137) This marked a record seventh Super Bowl victory for [Tom Brady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Brady), also more than any individual NFL franchise, and who would also break his own record for the oldest quarterback to win a championship at 43 years old. On [February 12, 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVII), at [State Farm Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Farm_Stadium) in [Glendale, Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glendale,_Arizona), the Chiefs overcame a 10-point deficit at halftime to defeat the Philadelphia Eagles 38–35, winning Super Bowl LVII on a last-minute field goal. On [February 11, 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII), the Chiefs won Super Bowl LVIII at [Allegiant Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allegiant_Stadium) on an overtime touchdown. ## Venues To date only two teams have [qualified for a Super Bowl at their home stadiums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_curse#The_Home_Field_Advantage_Curse): the [2020 Tampa Bay Buccaneers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Tampa_Bay_Buccaneers), who won Super Bowl LV hosted at [Raymond James Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raymond_James_Stadium) (selected on May 23, 2017), and the [2021 Los Angeles Rams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Los_Angeles_Rams) the following season, who won Super Bowl LVI at [SoFi Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SoFi_Stadium). ## Notes and references ### References 75. # Super Bowl Winners List
## Quick Answer
The Seattle Seahawks won the most recent Super Bowl LX in 2026, defeating the New England Patriots 29-13.

## Latest Championship Update
The New England Patriots and the Pittsburgh Steelers have won the most Super Bowls, with six wins each.

## Recent Super Bowl Champions (2020-2025)
### Super Bowl LIX - Philadelphia Eagles Victory
The **Philadelphia Eagles** won Super Bowl LIX in 2025, defeating the Kansas City Chiefs 40-22 in New Orleans. This ended the Chiefs' bid for three consecutive championships and marked the Eagles' second Super Bowl title, their first since 2018.

### Super Bowl LVIII - Kansas City Chiefs
Patrick Mahomes won his third Super Bowl MVP award.

### Super Bowl LVI - Los Angeles Rams
The Los Angeles Rams won their first Super Bowl since returning to LA, defeating the Cincinnati Bengals 23-20 at home in SoFi Stadium.

### Super Bowls LV & LIV
**2021 (LV):** Tampa Bay Buccaneers defeated Kansas City Chiefs 31-9, with Tom Brady winning his 7th championship.

The **Kansas City Chiefs** dominated the early 2020s with three Super Bowl victories in five years (2020, 2023, 2024) before falling to Philadelphia in 2025.

## Frequently Asked Questions
### Who won the most recent Super Bowl?
The Seattle Seahawks won Super Bowl LX in 2026, defeating the New England Patriots 29-13 in Santa Clara. This was the Seahawks second Super Bowl championship win, after winning its first Super Bowl in 2014.
